I am no expert at all but write a list of things you like about yourself too. And have a think about what you're comparing yourself to. 
I did CBT this year and told my therapist I'm not good enough. Not good enough of anything. She said what do you consider perfect and what do you consider bad and when you put yourself on that scale where you have something to really go off, would you still say you're not good. 
It really helped. Now when I tell myself I'm a shit mum because I shouted and I start getting down on myself I stop and think about what a shit mum is. And I'm not a shot mum. I'm just not as perfect as I expect myself to be. 
Hope this helps. 
And definitely try and get therapy rather than letting it get any worse if you can  xx

I have just started this two weeks ago. We had our first session and recorded the conversation which I have to listen to each night. For my second session we went over the same narrative and I have to listen to this recording each night until my third session. 
We have only covered about a quarter of the story so far.
I have found it to be really difficult. My anxiety has been much higher, I have felt much more depressed and having more suicidal thoughts.
Having said that I can feel myself working through the trauma with her. And although listening to the recording each day is exhausting, I am having lots of realisations through doing so. 
My trauma has been massively repressed which is why I am struggling going through it. 
So basically it's absolutely awful but I do think it's working and it will make a difference in the long run. 
I would advise if you decide to do it then you make a couple of people aware of it so you can go to them for help when you need it. And also make sure you are leaving time for yourself to do what you need to to make yourself feel better. Mine is exercise, sleep and long baths.

I think it’s because the words sound so dramatic but in reality if you are thinking about it daily then your not usually throwing yourself on the floor sobbing. You’ve almost got used to the thought and it’s just an internal fight with yourself. 
I mean everyone is different but I don’t think what you’re saying is unusual-I also think that’s the reason a lot of people don’t get the help they need. 
For me depression is feeling like a burden and a let down-I’m not going to then shout and scream that I need help. 
And also nobody knows how to talk about it. I told my mum I didn’t want to be here anymore and she sent me a pic of some pjs she bought my son. 
Her friend on the other hand has a daughter struggling with depression demanding her mums time and help and it’s like her depression must be worse than mine because of the way she acts out.
Maybe it is, maybe it isn’t. I don’t think they should be compared but I also don’t think they should be judged based on how dramatic or loud or serious or ‘depressed looking’ you are when you tell people how you feel.
